title: [YouPass Collect] - UK University Student Distribution by Study Mode & Gender
prompt: The tables below show the distribution of students at UK universities by mode of study and gender. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The tables compare the numbers of male and female postgraduate students enrolled in full-time and part-time programs at UK universities over four academic years from 1996/97 to 2009/10.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, full-time enrolment increased substantially for both genders during the period shown, while part-time figures fluctuated. Additionally, female part-time students constituted the largest group in most years, though full-time students of both genders experienced the most dramatic growth.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding full-time students, in 1996/97, there were 75,370 male postgraduates studying full-time, approximately 13,000 more than their female counterparts at 62,344. The number of male full-time students subsequently rose steadily, reaching 87,070 in 2000/01, before surging to 115,550 by 2005/06 and ultimately doubling to 151,275 by the end of the period. A similar upward trajectory was observed for female full-time students, whose numbers climbed to 85,215 in 2000/01, then to 118,675 in 2005/06, before ending at 146,980 in 2009/10, representing more than a two-fold increase.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for part-time enrolment, male part-time students numbered 113,961 in 1996/97, slightly higher than female part-time students at 108,702. However, the male figures fluctuated considerably over the period, initially declining to 108,770 in 2000/01, then rising to a peak of 138,505 in 2005/06, before falling back to 117,105 by 2009/10. Meanwhile, female part-time numbers followed a less volatile pattern, increasing steadily to 125,855 in 2000/01 and peaking at 172,640 in 2005/06, before experiencing a modest decline to 163,340 in the final year.
